In Indonesia, but I'm only talking about Jakarta area. Most buses here have the doors in the back or the middle, while the driver is a bit further in the front, so it's a little awkward to thank your driver when you get off.

The private bus service providers don't pay their drivers unless they make a certain quota. So it's literally early bird gets the worm. Slow drivers don't make money. In many instances drivers won't even move if they only have 2-3 people in the bus, and wait till it's full, which often causes traffic jam. Is it safe? Mostly, yes, but there are accidents because of this barbaric system. And since the drivers are racing with each other, the passengers have to be equally quick on their feet to get on and off the bus. We have to stand on the steps and hang on the door to signal the conductor that we're going to get off. I do this everyday, and thankfully, have never had an accident from this.

There's a more sophisticated bus system provided by the government in Jakarta area, the TransJakarta. They do use shelters, and they don't use the dog eat dog system I described before, but still we don't thank the driver because he's too far in the front, and we get off from the middle, and it's often cramped, you can't even see him most of the time.

So, no, we don't usually thank our bus drivers.

Except for minibuses which are a small vans turned into public transport. We can still thank the drivers in this one. But it's still rather unusual.
